text: The model flagged this applicant as high‑risk because two of the three factors it looks at are pushing the default probability upward. First, the applicant’s revolving‑credit utilization is about 69 % of the available limit. Using that much of the credit line is a strong signal that the borrower may be stretched thin, and it contributed roughly +0.78 to the risk score. Second, the applicant is 28 years old. Younger borrowers statistically default more often, adding about +0.48 to the risk. The only mitigating element is that the applicant has no recent 30‑ to 59‑day past‑due accounts, which pulls the score down a small amount (‑0.15). The net effect of the high utilization and young age outweighs the modest positive factor, leading the model to assign a 52.2 % default probability and label the case as HIGH RISK.
